_comment: Curated layer for the `surface` section of docs/capabilities.json (discoverability-design.md §1.2). NOTE the honest boundary: stapel-agent's capabilities.json is otherwise still HAND-WRITTEN — this module has no gate registry and no docs/schema.json, so provides/axes/extension_points/operations_total are not derived from code and are not drift-gated. `make contract` patches in the two derivable things: module/version from pyproject (the hand-written copy had rotted to 0.2.10 against a 0.8.0 package) and the derived `surface`. Converting the rest of the document to an emitter is separate work.

redaction_gate.intent: Call before writing ANY model-produced text to a durable artifact (prompt log, cache row, transcript, report): raises RedactionError when the payload carries a provider key or the value of a *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_PASSWORD env var. It is a gate, not a filter — there is nothing to inspect afterwards, so an import without a call is the whole failure mode (that is exactly how it was lost once during a port: the import survived, the call did not).

detect_pwned_markers.intent: The FLAG half of the flag/escape split: report which known prompt-injection markers a piece of untrusted text carries, without deciding any encoding. Run it on every LLM output and every retrieved chunk before that text reaches a consumer; the SafetyReport is what a caller branches on.

redact_markers.intent: The ESCAPE half for auto-escaping template engines (Jinja2): strips injection markers and does NO entity encoding, because the template engine already encodes and pre-encoding here double-escapes. Use this — not a hand-rolled replace — for any text rendered into a template.

sanitize_for_rag.intent: The ESCAPE half for text fed BACK into a model: strips markers and collapses whitespace. Mandatory for every retrieval chunk — an unfiltered marker inside a RAG chunk lands in the follow-up model's context and re-triggers the same attack, so 'the reader already flagged it' is not a reason to skip this.
